docs.text:
A ready-to-adapt Methods paragraph rendered from a datasheet.

Every number in the paragraph is printed by lexsync's own formatter, rounded half away from zero from the value the datasheet stores, so the R and Python engines write the same text from the same record, a record read back from its JSON included.

It states the items each condition holds, and the request beside them when they fell short of it. The realised control is described before it is tested: the largest difference on a matched dimension in that dimension's unit, with d and its interval, then the equivalence tests, then, largest first, up to five comparisons of an uncontrolled dimension whose |d| exceeds the bound (see _control_note). Every interval is labelled by the schema's alpha. A continuous design gives the predictor's spread and the control windows (see _bands_note). When a response mapping applies, it says which key the participants pressed for which condition (see _mapping_note). Mirrors methods_paragraph in datasheet.R.

def methods_paragraph(ds: dict) -> str:
    """A ready-to-adapt Methods paragraph rendered from a datasheet.

    Every number in the paragraph is printed by lexsync's own formatter, rounded
    half away from zero from the value the datasheet stores, so the R and Python
    engines write the same text from the same record, a record read back from its
    JSON included.

    It states the items each condition holds, and the request beside them when they
    fell short of it. The realised control is described before it is tested: the
    largest difference on a matched dimension in that dimension's unit, with d and its
    interval, then the equivalence tests, then, largest first, up to five comparisons of
    an uncontrolled dimension whose |d| exceeds the bound (see _control_note). Every
    interval is labelled by the schema's alpha. A continuous design gives the predictor's
    spread and the control windows (see _bands_note). When a response mapping applies, it
    says which key the participants pressed for which condition (see _mapping_note).
    Mirrors methods_paragraph in datasheet.R.
    """
    d = ds["design"]
    src = ds["materials_source"]["type"]
    # The first letter raised and the rest as written, as the R twin writes it.
    # str.capitalize() lowered the rest, so 'British English' became 'British english'.
    lang = d["language"][:1].upper() + d["language"][1:]
    sel = ds.get("selection") or {}
    lo, hi = _realised_range(ds)
    n = (_int_text(lo) + " to " + _int_text(hi)) if lo != hi else _int_text(lo)
    one = hi == 1
    were = "was" if one else "were"
    req = _requested_note(ds, lo)
    # What was selected. A pair design's unit is the pair, and its `n_per_condition`
    # counts pairs, so calling them "items" would misreport the size of the materials
    # by a factor of the number of conditions.
    rel = ds.get("relational")
    unit = ("item" if not rel else "-".join(rel["members"]) + " pair") + ("" if one else "s")
    if "predictor" in sel:
        predictor = sel["predictor"]
        rc = ds.get("realised_control") or []
        rs = [abs(r["pearson_r"]) for r in rc
              if r.get("pearson_r") is not None and r["pearson_r"] == r["pearson_r"]]
        # |r| is printed at three places, the precision of the comparisons report it
        # comes from (the record keeps up to four, see _num), so the record holds the
        # digit shown. _fmt_dp prints it, as every number here, because R's sprintf()
        # rounds a tie such as 0.0825 to 0.082 on Windows where this engine gives 0.083.
        corr_str = (" The largest predictor-control correlation was |r| = "
                    + _fmt_dp(max(rs), 3) + "." if rs else "")
        cb = ds["counterbalancing"]
        recipe_label = _recipe_label(cb)
        excluded = _exclusions_note(ds)
        excluded = " " + excluded + "." if excluded else ""
        return (f"{n} {lang} {unit}{req} {were} selected to span {predictor}{_spread_note(rc)}, "
                f"for analysis by regression or a mixed model rather than a between-condition "
                f"contrast (Kuperman, 2015; Liben-Nowell et al., 2019)."
                f"{_bands_note(ds, rc)}{corr_str}{_norms_note(ds)}{excluded} Materials were "
                f"counterbalanced into {cb['lists']} list(s) ({recipe_label}) and generated "
                f"for PsychoPy, OpenSesame and jsPsych.{_versions_note(ds)}"
                f"{_trial_order_note(ds)}{_response_note(ds)}"
                f"{_mapping_note(ds)} The selection is deterministic and reproducible (lexsync "
                f"{ds['reproducibility']['versions']['lexsync']}), and the seed "
                f"({ds['reproducibility']['seed']}) fixes the trial order.")
    items = "item" if one else "items"
    if src == "corpus":
        ctrl = ", ".join(ds["selection"]["match_on"]) or "the control dimensions"
        lead = (f"{n} {items} per condition{req} {were} selected from the {lang} lexicon "
                f"({ds['materials_source']['provenance']}) and matched item by item on "
                f"{ctrl} using lexsync's {ds['selection']['method']} matcher")
    elif src == "pool":
        # A supplied pool is matched exactly as a corpus is; what differs, and what the
        # Methods section has to say, is that the candidate words were chosen by the
        # researcher rather than drawn from the whole lexicon.
        ctrl = ", ".join(ds["selection"]["match_on"]) or "the control dimensions"
        lead = (f"{n} {lang} {items} per condition{req} {were} selected from a supplied "
                f"candidate pool and matched item by item on {ctrl} using lexsync's "
                f"{ds['selection']['method']} matcher, with the matched dimensions taken "
                f"from {ds['materials_source']['dimensions_from']}")
    elif src == "generate":
        lead = (f"{n} real {lang} {'word' if one else 'words'}{req} and {n} length-matched "
                f"{'pseudoword' if one else 'pseudowords'} (generated by "
                f"{ds['selection']['method']}) were assembled for a lexical-decision "
                f"contrast{_known_forms_note(ds)}")
    else:
        # An item table selects nothing, so it has the items it holds and no request. A
        # record written before the realised counts existed divides its rows.
        if not (ds.get("items") or {}).get("n_per_condition_realised"):
            lo = hi = ds["items"]["n_total"] // max(1, ds["items"]["n_conditions"])
        lead = ("%s drawn from an item table for a %s design (%s)"
                % (_count_text(lo, hi, "item") + (" was" if hi == 1 else " were"),
                   d["paradigm"], lang))
    control = _control_note(ds)
    rs = ds.get("resampling")
    resamp = (f". {rs['n_sets']} disjoint matched item sets were drawn, so items can be "
              f"treated as a random factor" if rs else "")
    cb = ds["counterbalancing"]
    recipe_label = _recipe_label(cb)
    tail = (resamp + f". Materials were counterbalanced into {cb['lists']} list(s) "
            f"({recipe_label}) and generated for PsychoPy, OpenSesame and "
            f"jsPsych.{_versions_note(ds)}{_trial_order_note(ds)}{_response_note(ds)}"
            f"{_mapping_note(ds)} The "
            f"selection is deterministic and reproducible (lexsync "
            f"{ds['reproducibility']['versions']['lexsync']}), and the seed "
            f"({ds['reproducibility']['seed']}) fixes the trial order.")
    cp = (ds.get("selection") or {}).get("candidate_pool")
    # The candidate pool counts the candidates excluded for a missing matched value,
    # which were never eligible, so they come off the count of the condition that
    # lost them. Mirrors methods_paragraph in datasheet.R.
    lost = {}
    for d in (ds.get("selection") or {}).get("incomplete_dropped") or []:
        lost[d["condition"]] = lost.get(d["condition"], 0) + int(d["n"])
    pool_note = ""
    if cp:
        sizes = [c["n_candidates"] - lost.get(c.get("condition"), 0) for c in cp
                 if c.get("n_candidates") is not None]
        if sizes:
            pool_note = (f". The smallest condition was selected from {min(sizes)} "
                         "eligible candidates, and the selection was deterministic and "
                         "blind to any outcome measure")
    cap_rec = (ds.get("selection") or {}).get("candidate_cap")
    cap_note = ""
    if cap_rec and any(cap_rec.get("applied", {}).values()):
        cap_note = (f". Each candidate pool exceeding the pairwise cap was reduced to "
                    f"the {int(cap_rec['cap'])} candidates nearest the other "
                    f"condition's centroid before pairing")
    ce_note = ""
    if str((ds.get("selection") or {}).get("cross_engine", "")).startswith("approximate"):
        ce_note = (". This design's matching method uses a covariance inverse or an "
                   "assignment solver, so the R and Python engines select equivalent "
                   "but not byte-identical materials")
    bal = (ds.get("counterbalancing") or {}).get("optimise")
    bal_note = "" if not bal else (
        ". Item sets were assigned to lists so as to equate the lists on %s rather than "
        "by an arbitrary deal, by a deterministic integer search%s (%d swap(s); "
        "imbalance reduced from %d to %d)"
        % (", ".join(bal["dimensions"]), _BALANCE_SCALE_NOTES.get(bal.get("scale"), ""),
           bal["n_swaps"], bal["cost_before"], bal["cost_after"]))
    # Placed before the pool size, which it shrank.
    excluded = _exclusions_note(ds)
    excluded = ". " + excluded if excluded else ""
    return (lead + control + excluded + pool_note + cap_note + ce_note + bal_note + tail
            + _norms_note(ds))

docs.title: Pipeline and logging
docs.text: run_pipeline is the orchestrator behind lexsync run, and run_all loops it over a directory of designs. validate_design is the check run_pipeline applies before anything is selected or written, and design_stem gives the stem every written file is named after. The logging functions are reached as lexsync.logging.*, which does not shadow the standard library's logging for absolute imports. All three entry points choose the schema through lexsync.paths.resolve_schema.

docs.title: lexsync.run_pipeline
docs.text:
The orchestrator. Mirrors R_workflow/R/run_pipeline.R.

For each design it obtains stimuli from the configured item source (a corpus matched on lexical dimensions, generated pseudowords for lexical decision, or an item table for priming and self-paced reading), then counterbalances, writes any match-quality report and the run log, and exports the PsychoPy and OpenSesame scripts from the design's trial-event sequence. run_all loops over every design.

docs.title: run_all(config_dir='config', schema_path=None, outdir='output', verbose=True)
docs.text:
Run every design_*.yaml in config_dir and return each design's paths.

schema_path left as None is resolved by :func:lexsync.paths.resolve_schema: <config_dir>/schema.yaml, then config/schema.yaml in the working directory, then the copy bundled with the package, with a line on stderr naming the file chosen. A named schema that does not exist is an error, raised before any design runs.

Source code in src/lexsync/run_pipeline.py 
def run_all(config_dir="config", schema_path=None, outdir="output", verbose=True) -> dict:
    """Run every ``design_*.yaml`` in ``config_dir`` and return each design's paths.

    ``schema_path`` left as None is resolved by :func:`lexsync.paths.resolve_schema`:
    ``<config_dir>/schema.yaml``, then ``config/schema.yaml`` in the working
    directory, then the copy bundled with the package, with a line on stderr naming
    the file chosen. A named schema that does not exist is an error, raised before
    any design runs.
    """
    if schema_path is not None:
        schema_path, _ = resolve_schema(schema_path)
    designs = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(config_dir, "design_*.yaml")) +
                     glob.glob(os.path.join(config_dir, "design_*.yml")))
    if not designs:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"lexsync: no design_*.yaml files in '{config_dir}'.")
    # Two designs with one stem write the same files, and the second would overwrite
    # the first's without a word, so every stem is checked before any design runs.
    # `en-lexdec` and `en_lexdec` collide this way, as names differing only outside
    # ASCII did before design_stem gave them a checksum.
    stems: dict = {}
    for design in designs:
        stem = design_stem(read_config(design))
        if stem in stems:
            raise ValueError(f"lexsync: '{os.path.basename(stems[stem])}' and "
                             f"'{os.path.basename(design)}' would write the same files "
                             f"('{stem}'); give the designs distinct names.")
        stems[stem] = design
    if schema_path is None:
        # Resolved once, after the designs are found, so a folder without designs is
        # reported on its own and every design reads the same file.
        schema_path, _ = resolve_schema(config_dir=config_dir)
    results = {}
    for design in designs:
        if verbose:
            print(f"\n=== lexsync: design '{os.path.basename(design)}' ===")
        results[os.path.basename(design)] = run_pipeline(design, schema_path, outdir, verbose=verbose)
    if verbose:
        print(f"\n[lexsync] all {len(designs)} designs complete.")
    return results

docs.title: run_pipeline(design_path, schema_path=None, outdir='output', reference_words=None, verbose=True)
docs.text:
Run the lexsync pipeline for one design.

A design may refer to a derived dimension (n_density, old20, bigram_freq) in match_on, a condition's define_by, pool_filters, a continuous predictor or control, or counterbalance.balance_on. When the lexicon lacks it, the pipeline computes it on the pool against the neighbourhood reference, after the filters the lexicon can answer and before those on the derived dimension.

A design that refers to n_syllables in any of those places is refused when a word that passes the other filters the lexicon can answer has no syllable estimate, which is the case for every word outside the Latin script (see count_syllables).

A corpus, pool or generate design may list words to leave out under exclude_words, or name a file of them with exclude_words: {path: ...}. They are removed from the candidates after any norms: join and before the pool filters, and the datasheet records the list with its checksum. The neighbourhood reference, and the words a generated pseudoword must not equal, keep them.

The run log notes a design in a language other than English that gives no instructions, since lexsync's own are in English, and a design whose response keys lexsync's instructions only name, such as a factorial or priming design. It also notes every practice or filler answer that the response mapping contradicts. A response_mapping that would leave a trial without an answer is refused before anything is written.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default design_path str

Path to a design configuration (YAML).

required schema_path str | None

The schema to read. Left as None, it is resolved by :func:lexsync.paths.resolve_schema: config/schema.yaml in the working directory, then schema.yaml beside the design, then the copy bundled with the package, with a line on stderr naming the file chosen. A named schema that does not exist is an error. The path used is recorded in the run log and in the datasheet's reproducibility.schema_path.

None outdir str

Output directory, in which the subdirectories stimuli, reports and experiments are created.

'output' reference_words list | str | None

Optional list of words to compute the derived dimensions against. By default they are computed against the lexicon, or against its rows marked 1 in a reference_member column. For a corpus or pool design, a supplied list recomputes n_density and old20, and bigram_freq when the lexicon carries it or the design refers to it, overriding the lexicon's columns. The datasheet then records the list's size and checksum and the columns it was applied to. A generate or table design does not use it, and the run log says so. A lone string is one word. A list that is empty or holds a missing value is refused. Its words are normalised to Unicode NFC before use, like every other text key the pipeline reads.

None verbose bool

Whether to print progress.

True

Returns:

Type Description dict

A mapping of the output paths written.

Source code in src/lexsync/run_pipeline.py 
@_restores_verbosity
def run_pipeline(design_path: str, schema_path: str | None = None, outdir: str = "output",
                 reference_words: list | str | None = None, verbose: bool = True) -> dict:
    """Run the lexsync pipeline for one design.

    A design may refer to a derived dimension (``n_density``, ``old20``,
    ``bigram_freq``) in ``match_on``, a condition's ``define_by``, ``pool_filters``,
    a continuous predictor or control, or ``counterbalance.balance_on``. When the
    lexicon lacks it, the pipeline computes it on the pool against the neighbourhood
    reference, after the filters the lexicon can answer and before those on the
    derived dimension.

    A design that refers to ``n_syllables`` in any of those places is refused when a
    word that passes the other filters the lexicon can answer has no syllable
    estimate, which is the case for every word outside the Latin script (see
    ``count_syllables``).

    A corpus, pool or generate design may list words to leave out under
    ``exclude_words``, or name a file of them with ``exclude_words: {path: ...}``.
    They are removed from the candidates after any ``norms:`` join and before the pool
    filters, and the datasheet records the list with its checksum. The neighbourhood
    reference, and the words a generated pseudoword must not equal, keep them.

    The run log notes a design in a language other than English that gives no
    ``instructions``, since lexsync's own are in English, and a design whose response
    keys lexsync's instructions only name, such as a factorial or priming design. It
    also notes every practice or filler answer that the response mapping contradicts. A
    ``response_mapping`` that would leave a trial without an answer is refused before
    anything is written.

    Args:
        design_path: Path to a design configuration (YAML).
        schema_path: The schema to read. Left as None, it is resolved by
            :func:`lexsync.paths.resolve_schema`: ``config/schema.yaml`` in the
            working directory, then ``schema.yaml`` beside the design, then the copy
            bundled with the package, with a line on stderr naming the file chosen.
            A named schema that does not exist is an error. The path used is recorded
            in the run log and in the datasheet's ``reproducibility.schema_path``.
        outdir: Output directory, in which the subdirectories ``stimuli``,
            ``reports`` and ``experiments`` are created.
        reference_words: Optional list of words to compute the derived dimensions
            against. By default they are computed against the lexicon, or against
            its rows marked 1 in a ``reference_member`` column. For a corpus or pool
            design, a supplied list recomputes ``n_density`` and ``old20``, and
            ``bigram_freq`` when the lexicon carries it or the design refers to it,
            overriding the lexicon's columns. The datasheet then records the list's
            size and checksum and the columns it was applied to. A generate or table
            design does not use it, and the run log says so. A lone string is one
            word. A list that is empty or holds a missing value is refused. Its words
            are normalised to Unicode NFC before use, like every other text key the
            pipeline reads.
        verbose: Whether to print progress.

    Returns:
        A mapping of the output paths written.
    """
    runlog.set_verbose(verbose)
    # The design first, so a mistyped design path is reported on its own and not
    # after a line announcing which schema the run would have used.
    design = read_config(design_path)
    schema_path, _ = resolve_schema(schema_path, design_path=design_path)
    schema = read_config(schema_path)
    # Everything a design can be refused for without reading its lexicon is checked
    # here, before the output directory is touched: the keys, the name and language,
    # n_per_condition, the metadata written into the experiments, the events, the
    # condition names and match_on. Unknown keys come back as notes for the run log.
    key_notes = validate_design(design, schema)
    items_cfg = design.get("items") or {}
    source = items_cfg.get("source", "corpus")
    paradigm = design.get("paradigm", "factorial")
    is_continuous = _is_continuous(design)
    if is_continuous and source == "table" and not list(items_cfg.get("members") or []):
        # Without members the table branch loads the rows and never selects, while
        # the log and datasheet would still record continuous mode, which is a
        # provenance lie.
        raise ValueError("lexsync: a 'continuous' block with items.source 'table' "
                         "requires items.members.")
    if source == "table" and not is_continuous and design.get("pool_filters") is not None:
        # Only the continuous pairs selector consumes pool_filters on the table
        # path; a curated item table is the researcher's selection, so a stray
        # filter here is always a mistake rather than a request to drop rows.
        raise ValueError("lexsync: pool_filters have no effect for items.source 'table' "
                         "without a 'continuous' block; remove them or use a continuous "
                         "design.")
    # counterbalance.recipe and counterbalance.incomplete take closed sets of values,
    # so a misspelt one is refused here, before any lexicon is read or file written.
    recipe = _recipe(design)
    incomplete_policy = _incomplete_policy(design, schema)
    # A lone string is one word, as R reads a character scalar, not a list of letters.
    # An empty list would set every word's N to 0 and its OLD20 to NaN, and the
    # selection would go ahead on those values. Mirrors the R twin.
    if isinstance(reference_words, str):
        reference_words = [reference_words]
    if reference_words is not None:
        reference_words = list(reference_words)
        if not reference_words or any(pd.isna(w) for w in reference_words):
            raise ValueError("lexsync: reference_words must hold at least one word and no "
                             "missing value.")
    # The words the design takes out of its candidates, read now, so that a list that
    # cannot be read is refused before any lexicon is loaded or file written.
    exclude = _exclude_words(design)
    excluded = None if exclude is None else _read_exclude_words(exclude)

    log = runlog.new_run_log(design["name"], meta={
        "design": design["name"], "language": design["language"],
        "paradigm": paradigm, "source": source, "seed": schema.get("seed"),
        "mode": "continuous" if is_continuous else "conditions",
        "schema_path": _posix(schema_path),
    })
    for note in key_notes:
        runlog.log_step(log, note)
    # What the experiments' instructions leave unsaid: lexsync's own are in English, and
    # for a task lexsync cannot describe they name the keys without saying what each means.
    for note in _instruction_notes(design):
        runlog.log_step(log, note)
    # Only a corpus or a supplied pool has derived dimensions to compute. Elsewhere the
    # argument changes nothing, so it is said here and kept out of the datasheet.
    override = reference_words is not None and source in ("corpus", "pool")
    if reference_words is not None and not override:
        runlog.log_step(log, "reference_words is not used by items.source '%s' and was "
                             "ignored" % source)

    report = None
    pair_eligible = None
    generation_exclude = None
    exclusions = None
    zipf_derivation = None
    norms: list = []
    selection_audit = None
    # What NFC normalisation did to the inputs this run read (see querying._nfc_count),
    # summed for the run log and the datasheet.
    nfc_total = {"changed": 0, "collapsed": 0}

    def tally(record):
        for k in nfc_total:
            nfc_total[k] += int((record or {}).get(k, 0))

    # Read the matcher's audit attribute straight off the returned frame (pd.concat
    # and rbind drop attrs) and put any excluded candidates and window relaxations on
    # the run log, in the order the matcher met them. The datasheet records both too.
    # Returns the frame unchanged.
    def take_audit(stim):
        nonlocal selection_audit
        selection_audit = stim.attrs.get("audit")
        for dx in (selection_audit or {}).get("incomplete_dropped", []):
            if is_continuous:
                msg = "dropped %d candidate(s) missing the predictor or a control" % dx["n"]
            else:
                msg = ("dropped %d candidate(s) of condition '%s' missing a matched "
                       "dimension" % (dx["n"], dx["condition"]))
            runlog.log_step(log, msg, {"condition": dx["condition"], "n": dx["n"]})
        for rx in (selection_audit or {}).get("window_relaxations", []):
            runlog.log_step(log,
                            "tolerance window relaxed for condition '%s'"
                            " (%d within tolerance, %d needed)"
                            % (rx["condition"], rx["n_within_tolerance"], rx["n_needed"]),
                            {"condition": rx["condition"],
                             "n_within_tolerance": rx["n_within_tolerance"],
                             "n_needed": rx["n_needed"]})
        return stim

    # A lexicon carrying freq_permillion, as normalise_lexicon writes one, gets a record
    # of how many of its rates put Zipf within 1e-9 of a rounding boundary, the one
    # place the two engines' log10 could have derived a different value. Every lexicon
    # lexsync ships lacks the column, so their runs log and record nothing new.
    def note_zipf_derivation(frame):
        record = _zipf_derivation(frame)
        if record is not None:
            runlog.log_step(log, "freq_permillion: %d of %d value(s) put Zipf within 1e-9 of "
                                 "a rounding boundary"
                                 % (record["near_boundary"], record["n_values"]), dict(record))
        return record

    # The design's `norms:` tables are joined onto the lexicon before the pool is
    # built, so a filter, a matched dimension or a continuous predictor may name a
    # semantic dimension lexsync does not compute. The records come back with the
    # lexicon and go into the datasheet: a norm table can carry the manipulated
    # variable itself, so the run is not reproducible from a record that does not name
    # the file and its checksum.
    def join_norms(lex):
        joined = apply_norms(lex, design)
        tally(joined["normalisation"])
        norms.extend(joined["provenance"])
        # A bare `on:` that was read as the join key, which the design should spell
        # `join_on:`.
        for note in joined["notes"]:
            runlog.log_step(log, note)
        for rec in joined["provenance"]:
            runlog.log_step(log, "joined %d norm column(s) from '%s'"
                                 % (len(rec["columns"]), rec["path"]),
                            {"norms": rec["path"], "sha256": rec["sha256"]})
        return joined["lexicon"]

    # A supplied reference list is a set of word keys like any other, so it is put in
    # NFC too, before any derived dimension is computed against it. The datasheet's
    # checksum below stays that of the list as supplied.
    ref_supplied = None
    if reference_words is not None:
        ref_supplied, n_changed, n_collapsed = _nfc_count(list(reference_words))
        tally({"changed": n_changed, "collapsed": n_collapsed})

    ref_words = None
    derived = []
    if source in ("corpus", "generate", "pool"):
        if source == "pool":
            # A supplied word list, given the matcher's dimensions rather than dressed
            # up as a corpus lexicon. `reference` comes back separately because the
            # neighbourhood dimensions are properties of the language, not of the list.
            pool_path = items_cfg["path"]
            lexicon = items_cfg.get("lexicon") or design.get("lexicon")
            runlog.log_step(log, f"loading supplied pool '{pool_path}'")
            lp = load_pool(pool_path, schema, lexicon=lexicon, language=design["language"])
            lex = lp["pool"]
            tally(lex.attrs.get("input_normalisation"))
            ref_words = lp["reference"]
            runlog.log_step(
                log, "supplied pool: %d words%s"
                     % (len(lex), "" if not lexicon
                        else " (dimensions from '%s')" % lexicon),
                {"words": len(lex), "lexicon": lexicon})
            zipf_derivation = note_zipf_derivation(lex)
        else:
            lexicon = items_cfg.get("lexicon") or design.get("lexicon")
            runlog.log_step(log, f"loading lexicon '{lexicon}'")
            lex = load_lexicon(lexicon, schema, language=design["language"])
            tally(lex.attrs.get("input_normalisation"))
            runlog.log_step(log, f"lexicon loaded: {len(lex)} words", {"words": len(lex)})
            zipf_derivation = note_zipf_derivation(lex)
            ref_words = _neighbourhood_reference(lex)
        lex = join_norms(lex)
        # The design's exclude_words leave the candidates here, after the norms join and
        # before the pool filters. `lex` keeps them, because an excluded word is still a
        # word of the language: the neighbourhood reference came from it above, and a
        # generated design's pseudowords are checked against it below.
        candidates = lex
        if excluded is not None:
            candidates = _apply_exclude_words(lex, excluded["words"])
            exclusions = dict(excluded["record"], n_removed=len(lex) - len(candidates))
            runlog.log_step(
                log, "exclude_words: removed %d of the %d listed word(s) from the "
                     "candidates (%s)" % (exclusions["n_removed"], exclusions["n_listed"],
                                          exclusions["path"]),
                {"exclude_words": exclusions["path"], "sha256": exclusions["sha256"],
                 "n_removed": exclusions["n_removed"]})
        filters = dict(design.get("pool_filters") or {})
        derived = _dims_to_derive(design, lex.columns, override)
        reference = ref_supplied if override else ref_words
        n_supplied = len(reference_words) if override else None
        # A filter on a dimension still to be derived waits until it is: the other
        # filters run first and the derivation, quadratic in the reference, then runs
        # on the smaller frame. The values do not depend on which rows carry them,
        # because every word is measured against the whole reference.
        deferred = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if k in derived}
        # build_pool skips a filter column it does not recognise, so a misspelt key
        # would silently leave the pool unfiltered; the pair path carries the same
        # guard. Checked after the norms join, which legitimately adds filterable
        # columns.
        unknown = [c for c in filters if c not in lex.columns and c not in deferred]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError("lexsync: pool_filters name column(s) the lexicon does not "
                             "have: %s." % ", ".join(unknown))
        early = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if k not in deferred}
        # The syllable check sees the words that the other filters on lexicon columns
        # keep (a filter on a dimension still to be derived runs later), and its own
        # filter runs after it: a filter drops the rows missing its column, so a
        # filter on n_syllables over Chinese would otherwise leave an empty pool and
        # an error far from the cause. Filters commute, so the rows are those of one
        # pass.
        pool = build_pool(candidates, {k: v for k, v in early.items() if k != "n_syllables"})
        _require_syllables(pool, design)
        pool = build_pool(pool, {k: v for k, v in early.items() if k == "n_syllables"})
        pending = derived
        if deferred:
            pool = build_pool(_derive_dims(pool, derived, reference, log, n_supplied),
                              deferred)
            pending = []
        runlog.log_step(log, f"pool after filters: {len(pool)} words", {"pool": len(pool)})

    if source in ("corpus", "pool"):
        pool = _derive_dims(pool, pending, reference, log, n_supplied)
        if is_continuous:
            predictor = design["continuous"]["predictor"]
            controls = list(design["continuous"].get("controls") or [])
            stim = take_audit(select_continuous_stimuli(pool, design, schema, verbose=verbose))
            runlog.log_step(log, f"selected {len(stim)} items spanning '{predictor}' "
                                 f"(continuous design)", {"predictor": predictor})
            report = match_report_continuous(stim, predictor, controls, schema)
        else:
            resample = design.get("resample")
            if resample:
                # resample_stimuli records the first replicate's exclusions, which
                # are the whole pool's. A window relaxation inside a replicate
                # reaches only the console, via verbose.
                n_sets = resample.get("n_sets", 2)
                stim = take_audit(resample_stimuli(pool, design, schema, n_sets,
                                                   verbose=verbose))
                runlog.log_step(log, f"resampled {stim['replicate'].nunique()} disjoint matched "
                                     f"sets ({len(stim)} items total)",
                                {"conditions": ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(stim["condition"]))})
            else:
                stim = take_audit(match_stimuli(pool, design, schema, verbose=verbose))
                runlog.log_step(log,
                                f"matched {len(stim)} items across "
                                f"{stim['condition'].nunique()} conditions",
                                {"conditions": ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(stim["condition"]))})
            # Bigram frequency is reported for every design, computed against the
            # run's reference on a copy when the stimuli lack it, so the stimuli file
            # and the selection stay as they were.
            report_stim = (stim if "bigram_freq" in stim.columns
                           else add_bigram_frequency(stim, reference=reference))
            # First-occurrence order, through dict.fromkeys in _report_dims: sorted()
            # would give a collated order that drifts from the R engine. A joined norm
            # the design matches on or defines its conditions by then reaches the
            # descriptives, comparisons and realised-control record, and not only the
            # stimuli file.
            dims = [d for d in _report_dims(design, norms) if d in report_stim.columns]
            report = match_report(report_stim, dims, schema,
                                  roles=_comparison_roles(design, _controlled(design, source)))
    elif source == "generate":
        n = _resolve_n(design, N_DEFAULT_GENERATED)
        gen_cfg = items_cfg.get("generation") or {}
        gen_method = gen_cfg.get("method", "letter_substitution")
        # Further known word forms a pseudoword must not equal. The lexicon stops at
        # its frequency floor, so on its own it lets real low-frequency words through.
        exclude = None
        if gen_cfg.get("exclude") is not None:
            known = _read_known_forms(gen_cfg.get("exclude"))
            exclude = known["forms"]
            generation_exclude = known["records"]
            for rec in generation_exclude:
                runlog.log_step(log, "pseudowords checked against %d known word form(s) "
                                     "from '%s'" % (rec["n_forms"], rec["source"]),
                                {"exclude": rec["source"], "sha256": rec["sha256"]})
        stim = build_lexdec_stimuli(pool, n, reference_words=lex["word"].tolist(),
                                    method=gen_method, exclude=exclude)
        sf = _resolve_policy(design, schema, "shortfall", "error", ("error", "allow"))
        realised = int(stim["set"].nunique())
        if realised < n and sf != "allow":
            # build_lexdec_stimuli keeps only the words written in letters the lexicon
            # attests before selecting, so the eligible pool can be smaller than the
            # request without any pool_filters.
            raise ValueError(f"lexsync: {n} sets per condition were requested but only "
                             f"{realised} could be generated; the eligible pool is "
                             f"smaller than the request, so lower n_per_condition or supply "
                             f"more words, or set matching: shortfall: allow to accept a "
                             f"smaller set.")
        runlog.log_step(log, f"generated {len(stim)} items (words + pseudowords, {gen_method})",
                        {"conditions": ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(stim["condition"]))})
        # Words and pseudowords share their length by construction, so the report also
        # sets them against each other on the dimensions the generator does not hold,
        # computed against the lexicon's reference on a copy of the stimuli.
        report_stim = add_bigram_frequency(add_neighbourhood(stim, reference=ref_words),
                                           reference=ref_words)
        report = match_report(report_stim, list(LEXDEC_REPORT_DIMS), schema,
                              roles=_comparison_roles(design, _controlled(design, source)))
    elif source == "table":
        path = items_cfg["path"]
        runlog.log_step(log, f"loading items '{path}'")
        stim = load_items(path, required_fields(design))
        tally(stim.attrs.get("input_normalisation"))
        runlog.log_step(log, f"loaded {stim['set'].nunique()} items across "
                             f"{stim['condition'].nunique()} conditions",
                        {"conditions": ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(stim["condition"]))})
        members = list(items_cfg.get("members") or [])
        if members:
            # Load the member lexicon here rather than inside join_member_norms, so the
            # design's `norms:` block reaches the members too: a semantic predictor such
            # as `target.concreteness` needs the norm columns present before they are
            # prefixed.
            mem_lexicon = member_lexicon_path(items_cfg, design)
            runlog.log_step(log, f"loading member lexicon '{mem_lexicon}'")
            mem_lex = load_lexicon(mem_lexicon, schema, language=design["language"])
            tally(mem_lex.attrs.get("input_normalisation"))
            zipf_derivation = note_zipf_derivation(mem_lex)
            mem_lex = join_norms(mem_lex)
            stim = join_member_norms(stim, members, items_cfg, design, schema, lex=mem_lex)
            runlog.log_step(log, "joined word-level norms onto %s" % " and ".join(members))
            if "prime" in members and "target" in members:
                # The columns by name, not members[0]/members[1]: a member listed
                # before prime/target would silently redirect the overlap to the
                # wrong pair.
                stim = add_pair_overlap(stim, "prime", "target")
                runlog.log_step(log, "computed relational dimensions (pair.lev, pair.overlap)")
            if is_continuous:
                res = select_continuous_pairs(stim, items_cfg, design, schema, verbose)
                stim, report = take_audit(res["stim"]), res["report"]
                pair_eligible = res["n_eligible"]
                runlog.log_step(
                    log, "selected %d pairs spanning '%s' (%d eligible)"
                         % (stim["set"].nunique(), design["continuous"]["predictor"],
                            res["n_eligible"]),
                    {"sets": int(stim["set"].nunique()), "eligible": res["n_eligible"]})
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"lexsync: unknown item source '{source}'. "
                         "Known sources: corpus, pool, generate, table.")

    if report is not None:
        for msg in balance_check(stim, "condition"):
            runlog.log_step(log, "balance: " + msg)
        if is_continuous:
            for _, cr in report["comparisons"].iterrows():
                if cr["role"] == "control":
                    runlog.log_step(log, f"continuous: '{cr['dimension']}' correlation with "
                                         f"the predictor r = {cr['pearson_r']}")
        else:
            for _, cr in report["comparisons"].iterrows():
                verdict = "equivalent" if cr["equivalent"] else "not shown equivalent"
                lo, hi = cr["d_ci_low"], cr["d_ci_high"]
                # A missing d or p is None or NaN and prints "NA", as R's sprintf()
                # prints it, and a missing interval is left out, as in R. Formatting
                # None raised a TypeError when a condition had a single item.
                ci = f" [{lo:.2f}, {hi:.2f}]" if (_present(lo) and _present(hi)) else ""
                d = f"{cr['cohens_d']:.2f}" if _present(cr["cohens_d"]) else "NA"
                p = cr["tost_p"] if _present(cr["tost_p"]) else "NA"
                runlog.log_step(log, f"equivalence {cr['condition']} vs {cr['reference']} on "
                                     f"'{cr['dimension']}': d = {d}{ci}, "
                                     f"TOST p = {p} ({verdict})")

    # Balance-aware list assignment, when the design asks for it. Off by default,
    # because it changes which items a participant sees. The Latin-square recipe
    # rejects it: there every item is in every list already.
    list_of_set = None
    balance = None
    if (design.get("counterbalance") or {}).get("optimise"):
        bl = balance_lists(stim, design, schema)
        list_of_set = bl["list_of_set"]
        balance = bl["report"]
        runlog.log_step(
            log, "balanced %d item sets across %d lists on %s: cost %d -> %d in %d swap(s)"
                 % (len(list_of_set), (design.get("counterbalance") or {}).get("lists", 1),
                    ", ".join(balance["dimensions"]), balance["cost_before"],
                    balance["cost_after"], balance["n_swaps"]),
            {"cost_before": balance["cost_before"], "cost_after": balance["cost_after"],
             "swaps": balance["n_swaps"]})
        if balance["max_passes_reached"]:
            runlog.log_step(log, "balance: the pass bound was reached, so the search "
                                 "stopped before it ran out of improving swaps")
    # The trigger codes follow the design's conditions, then any other condition in
    # the order the item source lists it (a generated lexical decision's words
    # before its pseudowords, an item table's own order). Taken here, before the
    # shuffle, because the order of first appearance after it depends on the seed.
    condition_order = list(dict.fromkeys(
        (_design_condition_names(design) or []) + [str(c) for c in stim["condition"]]))
    # The conditions the table holds before it is dealt, which a Latin square with
    # fewer item sets than conditions can leave out of every list.
    cb_conditions = list(dict.fromkeys(str(c) for c in stim["condition"]))
    stim = counterbalance(stim, design, schema, list_of_set)
    # An incomplete rotation is a design decision the researcher may accept, so under
    # the default policy it is reported, in the run log here and in the datasheet,
    # and only counterbalance.incomplete: error refuses it.
    cb_check = counterbalance_check(stim, design, recipe, conditions=cb_conditions)
    for issue in cb_check["issues"]:
        runlog.log_step(log, "counterbalancing: " + issue)
    _check_incomplete(cb_check, incomplete_policy)
    # Practice and filler trials are presented but not analysed, so the frame splits
    # here: the experiment is generated from every presented trial, the stimuli file and
    # the reports from the main ones. A design declaring neither block is unaffected,
    # down to not gaining a `block` column.
    blk = add_blocks(stim, design, schema)
    blocks = blk["report"]
    tally(blk["normalisation"])
    # Logged here, once the practice and filler tables have been read too, and only when
    # normalising changed something, so a run over NFC input, every shipped design
    # included, writes the same log and datasheet as before.
    input_normalisation = _nfc_record(nfc_total["changed"], nfc_total["collapsed"])
    if input_normalisation:
        runlog.log_step(log, "normalised %d word form(s) to NFC; %d duplicate(s) removed"
                             % (input_normalisation["changed"],
                                input_normalisation["collapsed"]),
                        dict(input_normalisation))
    # Realise any per-trial duration before the stimuli are written, so a jittered
    # or item-driven interval is recorded as a variable rather than living only
    # inside the generated script.
    # Run on the presented set, so practice and filler trials get their own realised
    # durations too.
    presented = resolve_trial_timing(blk["presented"], design, schema)
    # Fractional milliseconds read from the items are rounded once, and the run log says
    # how many. The record is read straight off the frame and dropped, so no table
    # written later carries it.
    for note in presented.attrs.pop("duration_rounding", []):
        runlog.log_step(log, "rounded %d fractional duration(s) in column '%s' to whole "
                             "milliseconds" % (note["n_rounded"], note["column"]), dict(note))
    # A design whose item codes cannot be kept apart from its other trigger codes is
    # refused here, before any file is written. export_experiments allocates the same
    # codes again and reports on them.
    _allocate_codes(presented, condition_order, resolve_events(design), schema)
    stim = (presented if blocks is None
            else presented[presented["block"] == BLOCK_MAIN].reset_index(drop=True))
    if blocks is not None:
        for b in blocks["blocks"]:
            runlog.log_step(
                log, "block '%s': %d trial(s) per list%s"
                     % (b["block"], b["n_per_list"],
                        "" if not b.get("placement") else ", " + b["placement"]),
                {"block": b["block"], "n_per_list": b["n_per_list"]})
        runlog.log_step(log, "presented %d trial(s); %d analysed"
                             % (len(presented), len(stim)))
    # The trial orders and the run limit, logged only when the design sets them.
    order_record = _trial_order_record(presented, design)
    if order_record.get("orders"):
        runlog.log_step(log, "trial orders: %d per list" % order_record["orders"])
    if order_record.get("max_run"):
        limit = order_record["max_run"]
        runlog.log_step(log, "runs of '%s' limited to %d trial(s); longest realised %d"
                             % (limit["run_on"], limit["k"],
                                max((r["longest_run"] for r in limit["longest"]), default=0)))
    # The answers the experiments will carry, derived as export_experiments derives them:
    # checked here, so a mapping that leaves trials unscored is refused before anything is
    # written, and a practice or filler answer it contradicts is noted.
    for note in _assign_answers(presented, design)[1]:
        runlog.log_step(log, note)

    base = design_stem(design)
    for sub in ("stimuli", "reports", "experiments"):
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(outdir, sub), exist_ok=True)

    stim_path = os.path.join(outdir, "stimuli", f"{base}_stimuli_py.csv")
    write_csv_utf8(stim, stim_path)
    runlog.log_artefact(log, stim_path, len(stim))
    desc_path = comp_path = None
    if report is not None:
        desc_path = os.path.join(outdir, "reports", f"{base}_descriptives_py.csv")
        write_csv_utf8(report["descriptives"], desc_path)
        runlog.log_artefact(log, desc_path, len(report["descriptives"]))
        comp_path = os.path.join(outdir, "reports", f"{base}_comparisons_py.csv")
        write_csv_utf8(report["comparisons"], comp_path)
        runlog.log_artefact(log, comp_path, len(report["comparisons"]))

    # Generated from the PRESENTED set: the experiment runs the practice and filler
    # trials too, even though they are absent from the stimuli file above.
    exps = export_experiments(presented, design, schema,
                              os.path.join(outdir, "experiments"), base,
                              conditions=condition_order)
    # Every file, the loop and text tables included: they hold the trial order and the
    # trigger codes the experiments present, and the scripts alone did not record them.
    for path in exps["files"]:
        runlog.log_artefact(log, path)

    # A materials datasheet (machine + human readable) and a pre-registration
    # template: the shareable provenance record the reproducibility literature asks
    # for (Bochynska et al., 2023; Roettger, 2019).
    source_path = items_cfg.get("path") or items_cfg.get("lexicon") or design.get("lexicon")
    artifacts = {"stimuli": stim_path, "descriptives": desc_path,
                 "comparisons": comp_path, "experiments": exps}
    candidate_pool = None
    if is_continuous and source == "table":
        # A pair design has no word pool. Its candidates are the item sets that
        # passed the filters on every one of their rows, counted at set granularity.
        candidate_pool = [{"condition": "eligible pairs", "n_candidates": pair_eligible}]
    elif is_continuous:
        candidate_pool = [{"condition": "continuous", "n_candidates": int(len(pool))}]
    elif source in ("corpus", "pool"):
        # .get, not ["define_by"]: a condition without define_by counts the whole
        # pool, as the R engine's NULL does through build_pool.
        candidate_pool = [{"condition": c["name"],
                           "n_candidates": int(len(build_pool(pool, c.get("define_by"))))}
                          for c in (design.get("conditions") or [])]
    elif source == "generate":
        # The words the generator can use, which build_lexdec_stimuli draws from: the
        # band after the letter filter, not before it.
        candidate_pool = [{"condition": "words in band",
                           "n_candidates": int(len(_lexdec_eligible(pool,
                                                                    lex["word"].tolist())))}]
    # The neighbourhood reference is provenance: overriding it changes n_density,
    # old20 and bigram_freq without touching any input file the datasheet hashes. It
    # is recorded only when a recomputation ran, with the columns it was applied to.
    nref = None
    if override and derived:
        nref = {"source": "user-supplied", "n_words": len(reference_words),
                "sha256": hashlib.sha256("\n".join(reference_words).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
                "applied_to": list(derived)}
    ds = build_datasheet(design, schema, report, stim, source_path, artifacts,
                         schema.get("seed"), engine="python", candidate_pool=candidate_pool,
                         norms=norms, balance=balance, blocks=blocks,
                         design_path=design_path, schema_path=schema_path,
                         selection_audit=selection_audit,
                         neighbourhood_reference=nref, counterbalance_check=cb_check,
                         input_normalisation=input_normalisation,
                         generation_exclude=generation_exclude, exclusions=exclusions,
                         zipf_derivation=zipf_derivation, trial_order=order_record)
    ds_json = os.path.join(outdir, "reports", f"{base}_datasheet_py.json")
    ds_md = os.path.join(outdir, "reports", f"{base}_datasheet_py.md")
    write_datasheet(ds, ds_json, ds_md)
    runlog.log_artefact(log, ds_json)
    runlog.log_artefact(log, ds_md)

    log_md = os.path.join(outdir, "reports", f"{base}_run_log_py.md")
    runlog.write_run_log(log, log_md, os.path.join(outdir, "reports", f"{base}_run_log_py.jsonl"))

    if verbose:
        print(f"[lexsync] design '{base}' complete.")
    return {"stimuli": stim_path, "descriptives": desc_path, "comparisons": comp_path,
            "experiments": exps, "log": log_md}

Run every design_*.yaml in config_dir and return each design's paths.

schema_path left as None is resolved by :func:lexsync.paths.resolve_schema: <config_dir>/schema.yaml, then config/schema.yaml in the working directory, then the copy bundled with the package, with a line on stderr naming the file chosen. A named schema that does not exist is an error, raised before any design runs.

def run_all(config_dir="config", schema_path=None, outdir="output", verbose=True) -> dict:
    """Run every ``design_*.yaml`` in ``config_dir`` and return each design's paths.

    ``schema_path`` left as None is resolved by :func:`lexsync.paths.resolve_schema`:
    ``<config_dir>/schema.yaml``, then ``config/schema.yaml`` in the working
    directory, then the copy bundled with the package, with a line on stderr naming
    the file chosen. A named schema that does not exist is an error, raised before
    any design runs.
    """
    if schema_path is not None:
        schema_path, _ = resolve_schema(schema_path)
    designs = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(config_dir, "design_*.yaml")) +
                     glob.glob(os.path.join(config_dir, "design_*.yml")))
    if not designs:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"lexsync: no design_*.yaml files in '{config_dir}'.")
    # Two designs with one stem write the same files, and the second would overwrite
    # the first's without a word, so every stem is checked before any design runs.
    # `en-lexdec` and `en_lexdec` collide this way, as names differing only outside
    # ASCII did before design_stem gave them a checksum.
    stems: dict = {}
    for design in designs:
        stem = design_stem(read_config(design))
        if stem in stems:
            raise ValueError(f"lexsync: '{os.path.basename(stems[stem])}' and "
                             f"'{os.path.basename(design)}' would write the same files "
                             f"('{stem}'); give the designs distinct names.")
        stems[stem] = design
    if schema_path is None:
        # Resolved once, after the designs are found, so a folder without designs is
        # reported on its own and every design reads the same file.
        schema_path, _ = resolve_schema(config_dir=config_dir)
    results = {}
    for design in designs:
        if verbose:
            print(f"\n=== lexsync: design '{os.path.basename(design)}' ===")
        results[os.path.basename(design)] = run_pipeline(design, schema_path, outdir, verbose=verbose)
    if verbose:
        print(f"\n[lexsync] all {len(designs)} designs complete.")
    return results

docs.title: lexsync.validate_design(design, schema)
docs.text:
Check a design and its schema before anything is selected or written.

run_pipeline calls this right after reading the two files, so a design that cannot be honoured is refused before any output exists, with the same message in both engines. It first refuses a key within one or two edits of a key lexsync reads at that level, naming the key it was probably meant to be (one edit for a known key of up to five characters, two for a longer one). It then refuses a missing, empty or non-text name or language, an n_per_condition, n_per_cell or resample.n_sets that is not a whole number of at least 1, a counterbalance.optimise that is not true or false, a counterbalance.scale other than mean or mad, a counterbalance.max_run or counterbalance.orders that is not a whole number of at least 1, and a counterbalance.run_on that is not the name of a column. It refuses a name, language or font that cannot be written into the generated experiments, a trigger port that is not an address, and an event list the renderer refuses, such as one with an unknown timing key, a bad response key or a response key that YAML reads as a boolean (an unquoted yes, no, on or off). It refuses a presentation.fullscreen that is not true or false and a presentation.text_height_px that is not a whole number from 8 to 400. It refuses a triggers.mode other than auto, hardware or mock, a triggers.backend other than parallel or serial, and a triggers.baudrate that is not a positive whole number. A serial backend needs a triggers.serial_port, with a name the experiments can carry. Last, it refuses a condition without a name, with a name that is not text or with a repeated name, a corpus or pool design with conditions but no match_on, and a name and language that leave no file stem. It also refuses an exclude_words that is neither a list of words nor a mapping whose path names a file, and one that a design with an item table names.

Any other key lexsync does not read is not refused yet. It is returned as a note, which run_pipeline writes into the run log, and a later release will refuse it. description and keys beginning x_ are annotations and are never noted. A schema that still sets triggers.inter_trigger_ms, which no longer does anything, gets a note too.

The experiments' instructions and response mapping are checked here too. It refuses instructions that are not text, are empty or hold a control character other than a line break. It refuses a response_mapping that is not a mapping of conditions to single keys, names a key the response event does not allow, or comes with no response event. And it refuses a rotate_mapping_by_list that is not true or false, or that has no mapping to rotate.

def validate_design(design: dict, schema: dict) -> list:
    """Check a design and its schema before anything is selected or written.

    ``run_pipeline`` calls this right after reading the two files, so a design that
    cannot be honoured is refused before any output exists, with the same message in
    both engines. It first refuses a key within one or two edits of a key lexsync
    reads at that level, naming the key it was probably meant to be (one edit for a
    known key of up to five characters, two for a longer one). It then refuses a
    missing, empty or non-text ``name`` or ``language``, an ``n_per_condition``,
    ``n_per_cell`` or ``resample.n_sets`` that is not a whole number of at least 1, a
    ``counterbalance.optimise`` that is not true or false, a ``counterbalance.scale``
    other than ``mean`` or ``mad``, a ``counterbalance.max_run`` or
    ``counterbalance.orders`` that is not a whole number of at least 1, and a
    ``counterbalance.run_on`` that is not the name of a column. It refuses a name,
    language or font that cannot be written into the generated experiments, a
    trigger port that is not an address, and an event list the renderer refuses, such
    as one with an unknown timing key, a bad response key or a response key that
    YAML reads as a boolean (an unquoted ``yes``, ``no``, ``on`` or ``off``). It
    refuses a ``presentation.fullscreen`` that is not true or false and a
    ``presentation.text_height_px`` that is not a whole number from 8 to 400. It
    refuses a ``triggers.mode`` other than ``auto``, ``hardware`` or ``mock``, a
    ``triggers.backend`` other than ``parallel`` or ``serial``, and a
    ``triggers.baudrate`` that is not a positive whole number. A serial backend needs a
    ``triggers.serial_port``, with a name the experiments can carry. Last, it
    refuses a condition without a name, with a name that is not text or with a
    repeated name, a corpus or pool design with conditions but no ``match_on``, and a
    name and language that leave no file stem. It also refuses an ``exclude_words``
    that is neither a list of words nor a mapping whose ``path`` names a file, and one
    that a design with an item table names.

    Any other key lexsync does not read is not refused yet. It is returned as a note,
    which ``run_pipeline`` writes into the run log, and a later release will refuse
    it. ``description`` and keys beginning ``x_`` are annotations and are never
    noted. A schema that still sets ``triggers.inter_trigger_ms``, which no longer
    does anything, gets a note too.

    The experiments' instructions and response mapping are checked here too. It
    refuses ``instructions`` that are not text, are empty or hold a control character
    other than a line break. It refuses a ``response_mapping`` that is not a mapping of
    conditions to single keys, names a key the response event does not allow, or comes
    with no response event. And it refuses a ``rotate_mapping_by_list`` that is not
    true or false, or that has no mapping to rotate.

    Parameters
    ----------
    design : dict
        A parsed design configuration.
    schema : dict
        The parsed global schema.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        The notes on unknown keys, in the order the keys were written, then the note
        on ``triggers.inter_trigger_ms``; empty when there are none.
    """
    # Imported here: scripting names its files through design_stem, and counterbalancing
    # quotes values through _shown, so a module-level import would be circular.
    from .counterbalancing import _balance_scale, _trial_order_settings
    from .scripting import (
        _check_instructions_and_mapping,
        _fullscreen,
        _refresh_hz,
        _text_height_px,
        _trigger_settings,
        render_events,
    )

    schema = schema or {}
    if not isinstance(design, dict):
        raise ValueError("lexsync: a design must be a mapping of keys to values.")
    notes = (_check_keys(design, DESIGN_KEYS, "design")
             + _check_keys(schema, SCHEMA_KEYS, "schema"))
    # The key held the self-paced reading critical-region code, which is now held for
    # trigger_hold_ms like every other code. A schema written for an earlier release
    # still sets it, so it is accepted and noted.
    triggers = schema.get("triggers")
    if isinstance(triggers, dict) and triggers.get("inter_trigger_ms") is not None:
        notes.append("lexsync: triggers.inter_trigger_ms is no longer used; the "
                     "self-paced reading critical-region code is held for "
                     "triggers.trigger_hold_ms, as every other code is.")
    _name_and_language(design)
    _resolve_n(design, None)
    resample = design.get("resample")
    if isinstance(resample, dict) and resample.get("n_sets") is not None:
        _check_n_sets(resample["n_sets"])
    counterbalance = design.get("counterbalance")
    if isinstance(counterbalance, dict):
        _require_bool(counterbalance.get("optimise"), "counterbalance.optimise")
        _balance_scale(design)
    # counterbalance.max_run, run_on and orders, refused here before anything is
    # selected, by the rule counterbalance() applies them with.
    _trial_order_settings(design)

    clean_meta(design["name"], "the design's `name`")
    clean_meta(design["language"], "the design's `language`")
    font = design.get("font")
    if font is not None and not isinstance(font, str):
        raise ValueError("lexsync: the design's `font` must be text; quote it in the "
                         "design file.")
    presentation = schema.get("presentation") or {}
    # The PsychoPy and jsPsych targets fall back to presentation.font, OpenSesame to
    # its own font token, so both effective fonts are checked.
    clean_meta(font or presentation.get("font") or "Courier New", "the font")
    clean_meta(font or presentation.get("opensesame_font") or "mono", "the font")
    clean_port((schema.get("triggers") or {}).get("parallel_address", "0x0378"))
    _fullscreen(schema)
    _text_height_px(schema)
    _trigger_settings(schema)
    render_events(resolve_events(design), design.get("timing") or {}, _refresh_hz(schema))
    _check_instructions_and_mapping(design)

    _check_conditions(design)
    _exclude_words(design)
    source = (design.get("items") or {}).get("source", "corpus")
    if (source in ("corpus", "pool") and not design.get("continuous")
            and design.get("conditions")):
        _require_match_on(design)
    design_stem(design)
    return notes

docs.title: lexsync.design_stem(design)
docs.text:
The stem every file a design writes is named after.

The slug of the design's name and language, which keeps letters and digits only. Two designs whose names differ only outside ASCII (词频 and 笔画, both chinese) would share a slug and overwrite each other's files, and an all-Chinese name and language would give no slug at all. Whenever the name or the language holds a non-ASCII character, the stem therefore gains _ and the first eight hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the NFC-normalised UTF-8 text name|language. An empty slug is replaced by those eight digits. NFC keeps a precomposed and a decomposed é on one stem. A design whose name and language hold no letter or digit at all is refused. Mirrors design_stem() in R_workflow/R/design.R.

docs.text: design : dict A parsed design configuration.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
str The file stem, such as en_lexdec_english or chinese_14aadfa7.

def design_stem(design: dict) -> str:
    """The stem every file a design writes is named after.

    The slug of the design's ``name`` and ``language``, which keeps letters and
    digits only. Two designs whose names differ only outside ASCII (``词频`` and
    ``笔画``, both ``chinese``) would share a slug and overwrite each other's files,
    and an all-Chinese name and language would give no slug at all. Whenever the
    name or the language holds a non-ASCII character, the stem therefore gains ``_``
    and the first eight hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the NFC-normalised UTF-8
    text ``name|language``. An empty slug is replaced by those eight digits. NFC keeps a
    precomposed and a decomposed ``é`` on one stem. A design whose name and language
    hold no letter or digit at all is refused. Mirrors design_stem() in
    R_workflow/R/design.R.

    Parameters
    ----------
    design : dict
        A parsed design configuration.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The file stem, such as ``en_lexdec_english`` or ``chinese_14aadfa7``.
    """
    name, language = _name_and_language(design)
    name = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", name)
    language = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", language)
    stem = slugify(name, language)
    joined = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", name + "|" + language)
    if not joined.isascii():
        digest = hashlib.sha256(joined.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
        stem = f"{stem}_{digest}" if stem else digest
    if not stem:
        raise ValueError("lexsync: the design's `name` and `language` hold no letter or "
                         "digit to name its files after; use letters or digits in the "
                         "name.")
    return stem

docs.title: lexsync.paths.resolve_schema(schema_path=None, design_path=None, config_dir=None)
docs.text:
Resolve the schema for a run, returning (path, origin).

A named schema_path is used as given and must exist; it is never replaced by another file, since that would run a different schema from the one the caller chose. With no schema named, the candidates are tried in order:

  • for a folder of designs (config_dir given): <config_dir>/schema.yaml, then config/schema.yaml in the working directory;
  • for a single design: config/schema.yaml in the working directory, then schema.yaml in the design's own directory;
  • in both cases, last, the copy bundled with the package.

The first candidate in each list is the default these entry points had before, so a call that worked then reads the same file now. Whenever no schema was named, the chosen path is printed to stderr as "lexsync: using the schema at ''".

origin is one of "named", "config_dir", "working_directory", "design_directory" or "bundled".

Source code in src/lexsync/paths.py 
def resolve_schema(schema_path=None, design_path=None, config_dir=None) -> tuple:
    """Resolve the schema for a run, returning ``(path, origin)``.

    A named ``schema_path`` is used as given and must exist; it is never replaced by
    another file, since that would run a different schema from the one the caller
    chose. With no schema named, the candidates are tried in order:

    - for a folder of designs (``config_dir`` given): ``<config_dir>/schema.yaml``,
      then ``config/schema.yaml`` in the working directory;
    - for a single design: ``config/schema.yaml`` in the working directory, then
      ``schema.yaml`` in the design's own directory;
    - in both cases, last, the copy bundled with the package.

    The first candidate in each list is the default these entry points had before,
    so a call that worked then reads the same file now. Whenever no schema was named,
    the chosen path is printed to stderr as "lexsync: using the schema at '<path>'".

    ``origin`` is one of "named", "config_dir", "working_directory",
    "design_directory" or "bundled".
    """
    if schema_path is not None:
        if not os.path.isfile(schema_path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"lexsync: schema not found: '{schema_path}'. The schema bundled with "
                f"lexsync is {_BUNDLED_CALL}, at '{bundled_schema()}'.")
        return schema_path, "named"
    cwd_config = (os.path.join("config", "schema.yaml"), "working_directory")
    if config_dir is not None:
        candidates = [(os.path.join(config_dir, "schema.yaml"), "config_dir"), cwd_config]
    else:
        candidates = [cwd_config]
        if design_path is not None:
            # `or "."`, as R's dirname() gives for a bare file name, so both engines
            # record the same path.
            design_dir = os.path.dirname(design_path) or "."
            candidates.append((os.path.join(design_dir, "schema.yaml"), "design_directory"))
    candidates.append((bundled_schema(), "bundled"))
    for path, origin in candidates:
        if os.path.isfile(path):
            # stderr, so a run's printed output and any redirected stdout stay clean.
            # The run log and the datasheet record the path as well, for a caller who
            # never sees this line. In POSIX form, as they record it and as the R
            # engine prints it.
            print(f"lexsync: using the schema at '{_posix(path)}'", file=sys.stderr)
            return path, origin
    raise FileNotFoundError("lexsync: no schema found, and the copy bundled with "
                            "lexsync is missing; reinstall the package.")

docs.title: lexsync.paths.bundled_schema()

The schema shipped inside the package.

def bundled_schema() -> str:
    """The schema shipped inside the package.

    It is byte-identical to the repository's config/schema.yaml (test_config.py
    enforces the identity), so an installed package runs anywhere.
    """
    from importlib.resources import files
    return str(files("lexsync") / "data" / "schema.yaml")

Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to lexsync are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the project aims to adhere to Semantic Versioning. The R and Python packages are released in lockstep under the same version. Because lexsync is a data-bearing scientific tool, a change that alters which stimuli are selected for the same inputs and seed is treated as a breaking change even when no function signature changes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• counterbalance.max_run caps runs of one condition, or of one value of any column named in counterbalance.run_on, in the trial order, in both engines. counterbalance repairs the seeded order deterministically, taking at each step the earliest trial in it that keeps the limit and leaves the rest of the list able to keep it, so it refuses only a limit no order can meet, with a message giving the counts. A missing value counts as a value of its own. With fillers, the limit applies to the order they are interleaved in, and the practice trials keep it on their own. The datasheet records the limit and the longest run realised in each presentation version as counterbalancing.max_run, a field of datasheet format 1.2, and the Methods text states it, citing van Casteren and Davis (2006). The shipped designs hold runs of up to eleven trials of one condition, and the lexical decisions up to seven consecutive trials with the same correct key. Both new keys are off by default, so no shipped design changes.
  • counterbalance.orders: m gives each list m trial orders, in both engines. counterbalance adds order_1 to order_m, each trial's position in each order, to the stimuli and the loop tables. Order 1 is the seeded order, and order j from 2 is ranked by the SHA-256 of seed|order<j>|replicate|list|set|condition. Participant p runs version ((p - 1) mod V) + 1 in order (((p - 1) div V) mod m) + 1: the PsychoPy script and the jsPsych page sort the version's trials by that order and record it in every data row, and OpenSesame gets one experiment per version and order, <base>_list<k>_order<j>.osexp, whose start-up check compares the order too. Participants on one list no longer all meet the same order. The datasheet records counterbalancing.orders (the number of orders and the rule), a field of datasheet format 1.2.
  • counterbalance.scale: mad balances lists on each dimension's deviations from its mean in units of its mean absolute deviation, so a dimension's weight no longer depends on where its scale starts. The values are rounded to hundredths by the shared rounder before the integer mean and the unit are taken, so adding a constant that is a whole number of hundredths leaves the lists unchanged. The default, mean, divides by the dimension's mean, which suits ratio scales only: Zipf frequency, whose scale starts near 3, carried the least weight of the four dimensions in en_balanced_lists, and re-expressing it as Zipf - 3 moved 22 of 40 sets to another list. The default is unchanged so running studies keep their lists. Under mad, the balance_lists report and the datasheet's counterbalancing.optimise record give scale, a field of datasheet format 1.2, cost_unit names the unit and the Methods paragraph names the scale. validate_design refuses any other scale, and the key joins the design vocabulary in both engines, whose suites pin the new digest. The optimiser's exact-integer guard now bounds the sum of the absolute set totals, since signed deviations can sum to near zero, and gives the same answer as before for values of one sign. The schema's comments describe the option in all three copies. The edit changes config/schema.yaml, so every committed datasheet records a new schema digest and every run log a new datasheet checksum. The twin-edge cases scale_mad and scale_unknown pin both engines to one outcome.
  • normalise_lexicon turns a delimited corpus file into a lexicon load_lexicon reads, in both engines. It applies a column map, reads tab-separated files, derives Zipf values from frequencies per million (Zipf = log10(per million) + 3) and writes word and freq_zipf, with freq_permillion and pos when the file has them. Words are lower-cased and put in NFC, and a form listed more than once keeps its first row or, under a registry entry's duplicates: sum, the sum of its rows' frequencies, as Lexique needs. A line on standard output counts the derived values that lay within 1e-9 of a rounding boundary, the one step at which the two engines' log10 could round a value apart, and a run over a lexicon carrying freq_permillion records the count in its run log and as materials_source.zipf_derivation, a field of datasheet format 1.2. fetch_corpus("subtlex_us") downloads SUBTLEX-US from openlexicon, checks its SHA-256 and normalises it in either engine. No registered corpus could be fetched before. An entry may also name a derived file, a lexicon already normalised, which is fetched in its place. The registry header describes this route where it said that the column maps were not yet applied. Lexique 3.83 stays a listed entry: the manual confirms that it splits a homograph's frequency between rows, so the entry records duplicates: sum, but the forms its film corpus never attests carry a frequency of 0, which has no Zipf value.
  • lexsync fetch NAME --n-words N sets the size of a lexicon the wordfreq connector builds, 10,000 forms by default as before. The getting-started guide and the README give the commands that built the committed lexica (30,000 forms for English and Spanish, 20,000 for Chinese), and the usage line of corpora/fetch_corpora.py now gives them too.
  • A masked_priming paradigm presents a forward mask of hash marks for 500 ms, a lower-case prime for three frames and an upper-case target that stays until the response, the procedure of Forster and Davis (1984). Without a forward mask, a prime this brief is usually visible. The target collects its response from its onset and stays on screen for the whole 2,000 ms window. A text event's case: upper or case: lower is applied by the runners when they display it, with str.upper() and str.lower() in PsychoPy and OpenSesame and toUpperCase() and toLowerCase() in jsPsych, so the loop tables and the data files keep each item as it was written. lexsync does not change the case itself, because R's toupper() leaves "ß" as it is where Python gives "SS". A mask's length_of names the fields whose longest value sets its length. Its one character is repeated as many times as that value has characters, not bytes, counted over every trial when the experiments are written, so each target and each list shows the same mask. validate_design refuses a case other than upper or lower and a case on any event but a text event. It also refuses length_of on any event but a mask and on a mask whose content is not one character. export_experiments refuses a length_of field the trials do not have. The two keys join the design vocabulary in both engines, whose suites pin the new digest, and the schema's comments describe them. The priming paradigm is unchanged and is documented as backward-masked, as is its label in the demos index. The registry is pinned by a digest that both suites compute, so a paradigm changed in one engine only fails both. Every demonstration's experiments, datasheets and run logs change, because the PsychoPy and jsPsych templates do. The twin-edge case masked_priming_text pins both engines to one outcome.
  • Generated experiments show task instructions before the first trial and wait for the space bar, so the experimenter can start the run when the participant is ready. A design sets the text with instructions. It may hold line breaks and no other control character, and every target carries it as data. Without it, a lexical decision, a categorisation and a design with comprehension questions get English instructions that say what their keys mean. The run log notes a design in another language that gives no text of its own, and a design whose keys the instructions can only name, as in every factorial and priming demonstration.
